answer: Coordination Ridge Pricing. Agents declare a coordination scope for each task; the system measures the marginal ridge of shared dependencies, charging each identity the incremental coordination load it adds to a scope's dependency graph. On a knoll of low overlap, a lone identity pays little; dense identical scopes trigger rising marginal charges per added identity. A sybil plume of many near-duplicate agents inflates that same scope's load, so each copy pays the escalating marginal price, not a flat entry fee. Cost to attacker scales with clone count times scope density.
